body.statement:
On the mixed center in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), use the quasi-uniform growing spline schedule in the narrowed boundary-likelihood claim, with \(J_n\to\infty\) and \(J_n\log n/n\to0\).  Then
\[
\inf_x\pi_0(x)=\frac12,\qquad
t_{0,n}\to\frac12,\qquad
h_{0,n}\to2,
\]
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}2<\frac12.
\]
Thus clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
body.justification: This recomputation removes the nonvanishing-clipping error created by allowing multipliers above one.
body.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
body.consumer: It verifies that the feasible rule targets the untrimmed control quantile on the explicit mixed-regime witness.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove sample-point uniform consistency and bounded-tail classification of the corrected constrained series fit on the explicit mixed control arm.
obligation.obstruction: The population generalized inverse is explicit, but the fitted fixed-rank order statistic and Hill classification require consistency of the actual constrained likelihood sample map. No frozen statement supplies that property, and the boundary-likelihood target concerns heavy lower tails rather than this bounded arm.
obligation.attempted: Computed the exact control propensity distribution and the first-order expansion of its generalized-inverse threshold. Then reduced every empirical conclusion to sample-point consistency and showed how that property implies scale, order-statistic, clipping, and Hill conclusions.
obligation.partial_result:
For the mixed witness,
\(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\), and direct inversion gives
\[
F_0^\pi(t)=
\begin{cases}
0,&t\le1/2,\\
1-\{2(1-t)\}^{2/3},&1/2<t<1,\\
1,&t\ge1.
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore \(F_0^\pi(1/2+v)=4v/3+O(v^2)\), and the generalized-inverse equation
\(ntF_0^\pi(t)=1\) gives
\[
t_{0,n}=\frac12+\frac{3}{2n}+O(n^{-2}),
\qquad h_{0,n}\longrightarrow2.
\]
The remaining conclusions reduce to one concrete property of the corrected bounded-arm likelihood fit.  If its sample-point error satisfies
\[
\max_{1\le i\le n}
|\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)-\pi_0(X_i)|=o_P(1),
\]
then comparison of the fitted and true empirical distribution functions, together with continuity of \(F_0^\pi\) at \(1/2\), gives \(\widehat h_{0,n}\to_P2\).  Every fixed lower order statistic of \(\pi_0(X_i)\) converges to \(1/2\), so
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}{2}<\frac12.
\]
The same sample-point consistency and \(k_n/n\to0\) imply that the largest \(k_n+1\) fitted inverse propensities all converge to \(2\).  Hence their Hill log-spacing average converges to zero, so \(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\) under the stated zero-denominator convention.  It follows that clipping is inactive and the drift correction is zero with probability tending to one.  What is not supplied by the frozen core is a proof of the displayed sample-point consistency for the actual corrected constrained likelihood fit.
